summary: Router 0.42.2 closes TM-08's next action 'bound chunked bodies per client' (ADR-0128, proposed, supersedes ADR-0063). Before, max_body_mib (default 16) was checked only against a declared Content-Length; a body sent with Transfer-Encoding: chunked was bounded only by the API app's client_max_size of 64 MiB, so a client could send four times its limit per request and up to max_concurrent such bodies. Now client_auth_middleware, for a configured client whose request has a body without a declared length, takes the client's concurrency slot first and then reads the body through request.clone(client_max_size=max_body) via the new boundary helper common.read_body_bounded, which reports BODY_READ, BODY_TOO_LARGE or BODY_UNREADABLE as a fact. aiohttp 3.14's BaseRequest.read checks the size while it reads (verified in its source), so memory per request stays within the limit plus one read chunk. BODY_TOO_LARGE answers 413 with the same message as for a declared size, counts too_large and writes the audit line body_too_large with chunked: true; the slot is given back in the existing finally. BODY_READ passes the clone (state incl. request['client'] and match_info copied by aiohttp) with the body cached and the fact request[BODY_PREREAD] = True, so handlers (read_json, request.read) see the full body; BODY_UNREADABLE passes the clone on and the handler's own read reports the failure as before (read_json -> None -> 400). Traced B1: identification, rate limit, inference refusal and the declared-size check run before as before; unauthenticated requests and the UI identity are unchanged (64 MiB ceiling). Request-body readers checked: proxy, openai_api, anthropic_api, rerank and admin read the whole body (read_json / request.read); session_api.body (used by the session API, memory.py and memory_gateway.py) streams request.content with its own 1 MiB bound and now uses the pre-read bytes when BODY_PREREAD is set, applying the same 1 MiB bound to them; managed.lines streams an upstream reply, not a request. For a chunked session or memory write from a configured client, memory per request is now the client's limit (default 16 MiB) instead of 1 MiB before the session bound applies; noted in ADR-0128. Exceptions: the helper catches aiohttp's HTTPRequestEntityTooLarge (the only signal aiohttp gives) and other read failures at the network boundary, both marked exception-ok; no error text is parsed. Possible behaviour change for operators: a client that sent chunked bodies above its max_body_mib now gets 413 (noted in the changelog with the fix: raise max_body_mib).

findings.evidence: The first version of this change pre-read chunked bodies in the middleware without telling handlers. session_api.body streams request.content itself, so a chunked session or memory write from a configured client would have found the stream used up and answered 400 'body must contain valid JSON' (reproduced by the new test with the session_api branch removed).
findings.resolution: The middleware sets the fact request[BODY_PREREAD]; session_api.body takes the cached bytes when it is set and applies its 1 MiB bound to them. test_handlers_that_stream_their_body_get_the_body_the_middleware_read covers a chunked JSON body (200), 2 MiB chunked (413 'session body exceeds 1 MiB') and a declared body (still streamed).

findings.evidence: An independent code review of PR #195 found that request.clone(client_max_size=...) does not exist in aiohttp 3.8.4 (checked in its source: clone has no such parameter; 3.9.1 has it), while router/requirements.txt allows aiohttp>=3.8.4 (Debian 12's python3-aiohttp). Every chunked request of a configured client would have raised TypeError there (500). CI runs aiohttp 3.14 only.
findings.resolution: common.CLONE_TAKES_BODY_LIMIT checks the clone signature once; common.with_body_limit uses the public parameter where it exists and otherwise clones and sets _client_max_size, the attribute aiohttp 3.8.4's read() checks (verified in its source; 3.8 refuses at >= the limit). test_the_limit_also_holds_where_clone_takes_no_limit forces the fallback: 17 MiB chunked 413, 3 MiB chunked 200 intact.

tests.evidence: 12 tests OK (also with the aiohttp 3.8 fallback path forced). New: 17 MiB chunked for a client with the default 16 MiB -> 413 with the client message, handler not run, too_large counted, audit body_too_large with chunked true, slot free (rejected case); 17 MiB chunked for a client allowing 32 MiB and a chunked JSON body reach the handler intact, also through read_json; session_api.body behind the middleware: chunked JSON 200, 2 MiB chunked 413, declared body unchanged; a slow chunked upload holds the client's only slot while it is read, a second request gets 429. Without the fix (auth.py from origin/main) the rejected case fails (200 != 413); with the pre-read moved before the slot (mutation) the slot test fails (0 != 1); without the session_api branch the session test fails (400 != 200).

tests.command: every python command of the python job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (Windows), except pip install, run_tests.py and check_public_changes
tests.evidence: 94 commands, 0 failed; includes check_control_flow (0 findings), ADR index (128), configuration check of config.example.yaml.
run after staging this record; added lines reviewed by hand: code, synthetic test values (example model/prompt), documentation.

limitations: Memory per chunked request is bounded by about twice max_body_mib: aiohttp raises its read chunk size to the limit and checks after appending a chunk.
The aiohttp 3.8 fallback was exercised by forcing it on aiohttp 3.14 (same attribute name in both, verified in 3.8.4's source), not on a real 3.8 installation.
Not measured under hostile load (many clients at once); TM-08's hostile-load test remains open.
Unauthenticated requests in observe mode and the router's UI identity keep the 64 MiB ceiling, as before.
ADR-0128 and router 0.42.2 are also taken by the open PR #194 (control UI CSP); the PR merged second renumbers (next free ADR number, next patch version).
